answers.evidence: The USB-C mouth is an open slot facing the camera in edge-J1.png.
The combo jack's round bore and contacts face the camera in edge-J101.png.
The barrel jack shows an open round recess with its centre pin facing the camera in edge-J106.png.
The 1/4in jack shows an open threaded nut with the contact visible inside in edge-J108.png.
The jack bodies and all other models sit over their pad patterns in iso, top and bottom, and none floats beside or below its pads, though the small parts are low resolution.
D2 and the five passives sit in one horizontal line with J1 centred directly above D2.
D106 and D105 sit side by side in a line with the same orientation, below the J106 pads.
The bootstrap cap sits above U103 while the other caps sit to its right, so the parts do not share one line.
L101, C114, C115 and C19 form a row, but U103 sits below and left of that row.
C20 sits left of U3 in line with it, but C23 sits below U3, so there is no single line.
L1, C21 and C22 form a row, but U3 sits above and left of it with another part between them.
C24, U4 and C25 sit on one horizontal line.
The ferrite, caps and resistors sit in one horizontal row right of the tantalum cap.
D3 and R10 share a row beside the inductor, but U3 sits well above and left of that row.
The caps and R1 sit scattered around Y1 on both sides and below it, not on one line.
The two caps are stacked vertically on U1's west flank at one x.
The FB1 and C8-C11 parts form a two-dimensional clump below U1's left side, not a column.
Several small caps sit south of U1 at mixed offsets, and with no highlight I cannot tell which are C4 and C7.
The caps on U1's east flank share one x and run in a vertical line.
The caps above U1's north edge sit on one horizontal line.
The crop has no highlight, so I cannot tell which parts are R27 and R29.
The crop has no highlight, so I cannot tell which parts are R30 and C55.
The two tact switches and the small part between them form a row far below and left of U1, and the C14 and R2 parts sit near U1 instead.
J3 sits directly left of U1 at roughly mid-height.
The LED and its resistor sit side by side on one horizontal line left of U1.
The leg runs vertically from the J101 pads down to U104 with parts on both sides, and it is not one horizontal row.
The mirror leg also runs vertically with side-by-side parts, so it is not one straight row.
The coupling caps and resistors surround U104 in stacked columns on both sides instead of one line.
The resistors sit in two columns on either side of U104, with the caps above and below.
The four resistors form a row below U105, but U105 sits above them and C127 sits to its right.
The small caps sit in a row above U105 while the electrolytic C159 sits off to the right, so there is no single line.
The parts right of U8 form a vertical column plus offset parts, not a horizontal row.
The supply parts around U8 are spread across several x positions, not one column.
The parts beside U6 sit in two or three offset columns rather than one.
The parts right of U6 are stacked vertically with offset neighbours, not a horizontal row.
The parts are scattered above, below and beside U106 in a two-dimensional spread.
The parts sit above and below U106 at different offsets, not on one line.
D104 sits left of the relay, but R120 and C162 are a vertical pair to its right.
The parts below K102 sit at different heights, with two stacked at the right.
The pull-up pairs sit at one y under each toggle, with a uniform pitch matching the toggles.
The filter caps share the same y under each toggle, at the same pitch as the toggles.
Four small parts sit in one horizontal row directly above the encoder.
Four small parts sit in one horizontal row directly above the encoder, matching the key encoder.
Four parts sit above the encoder and two below it, so they are on two rows.
The parts around U101 sit at scattered x and y positions, not in one column.
The two small caps sit in a row between pot rows but well off RV111's line.
The crop has no highlight, so I cannot tell which parts are the J117 pull-ups and which are neighbours.
The J101, J106 and J108 references read mirrored and upside-down, while all other refs read upright.
Only the three hand-soldered jacks (brief-exempt) appear on the bottom, and no bottom silkscreen is visible.
